resources.string: Performs Back, Home, and Recents when an edge zone is swiped.
Keeps the edge swipe overlays alive in the background.
Swipe up from a configured edge zone to trigger an action.
Enabled in Settings, but Android lost the binding after the last app update. Open Accessibility settings, toggle Ogesture off and back on.
Android only lets an accessibility service perform Back, Home, and Recents. Ogesture uses it for nothing else — it runs one of those actions when you swipe in from a screen edge.

Nothing is collected, stored off your phone, or shared with anyone. Ogesture has no internet permission, no ads, and no analytics. Your settings stay on this device and are deleted when you uninstall the app.
You can turn the service off at any time in Settings › Accessibility › Ogesture.
All set — flip the switch to start.
Edge gestures turned off: allow \"Display over other apps\".
Edge gestures turned off: the accessibility service isn\'t running.
Edge gestures turned off: allow unrestricted battery usage.
Edge gestures turned off: they can\'t run right now.
Granted — the system won\'t sleep the gesture service.
Required. Without this, Android or your phone\'s battery manager can kill the gesture service in the background, so gestures can\'t run reliably.
Also open Settings › Battery › Background usage limits and make sure Ogesture is not in the \"Sleeping apps\" or \"Deep sleeping apps\" list.
Also enable the \"Autostart\" permission for Ogesture in your phone\'s settings (on Xiaomi: Security app › Permissions › Autostart). Without it, the gesture service can be killed in the background.

Turn Ogesture off inside apps that ignore gesture taps.

A few apps may ignore the touches on gesture areas for security or other reasons. In those apps a tap near a screen edge may not work. Swipes for Back, Home, and Recents still work fine.\n\nIf dead taps bother you in an app, add it here — Ogesture will stay off inside that app.
No apps added yet — gestures are on everywhere.
Gestures also won\'t work on your phone\'s Settings app: Android hides overlay apps like Ogesture on Settings and other secure system screens. Use your phone\'s own navigation there.
Android\'s security policy blocks gestures on certain screens, such as your phone\'s Settings.
